newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels stock market seen rising after breather.
newsitem.headline: Brussels stock market seen rising after breather.

text.p: The Brussels bourse, which on Wednesday lagged its European neighbours as they moved higher, is expected to resume this year's heady climb on Thursday if, as expected, U.S. interest rates remain unchanged, traders said.
"The market expected the Fed to do nothing...and is getting ready to rise again," one trader said after the Bel-20 index added 3.94 points to 2,057.53 in a volume of 3.6 billion francs.

"The dollar is in our favour, long-term interest rates are in our favour and people still want to invest," another trader said. "We have consolidated a bit after January's strong rise and are now ready to move up."

Insurer Royale Belge, a premium financial stock on the Belgian bourse, finally ended a period of depression and surged 190 francs to 7,260 after hitting a new intra-day high of 7,300 francs on turnover of more than 24,000 shares.
Union Miniere took heart from the strong dollar, rising zinc prices and falling supplies of the metal and added 55 francs to 2,470 after also setting a new intra-day high of 2,485.
Traders said the share was also recovering after underperforming the market in recent weeks, although the full impact of the firm's restructuring would not be felt until 1999.
Chemical and drugs firm UCB, which reported a provisional 1996 pre-tax current profit approaching 5.5 billion francs after the market closed, ended the day 150 francs up at 94,450 francs.
The firm made current profits of 4.2 billion francs in 1995.
Chemical firm Solvay, which reports its provisional 1996 figures after the close of play on Thursday, suffered from mild position squaring and lost 175 francs to 22,300 francs.
Electronics firm Barco and retailer Delhaize both suffered mild profittaking.
